translation_en: Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: While a man was walking along a road, he found a thorny branch on it and moved it away. Allah appreciated this for him and forgave him.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: A man passed by a tree branch lying across a road and said: By Allah, I will move this away from the Muslims so it will not harm them. He was admitted to Paradise.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated this to us: Ubaydullah narrated to us: Shayban narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: I saw a man moving about in Paradise because of a tree he had cut down from the road that used to harm people.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: There was a tree that used to harm Muslims. A man came and cut it down, and he entered Paradise.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah asked: Who do you consider a martyr among you? They said: Messenger of Allah, whoever is killed in Allah's cause is a martyr. He said: In that case, the martyrs of my community would be few. They asked: Who are they, Messenger of Allah? He said: Whoever is killed in Allah's cause is a martyr; whoever dies in Allah's cause is a martyr; whoever dies of plague is a martyr; and whoever dies of a stomach illness is a martyr. Ibn Miqsam said: I testify, concerning your father in this hadith, that he said: And one who drowns is a martyr.

Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Wasiti narrated to me: Khalid narrated to us, from Suhayl, with this chain and a similar report. His hadith says: Suhayl said: Ubaydullah ibn Miqsam said: I testify about your father that he added to this hadith: 'Whoever drowns is a martyr.'

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us: Suhayl narrated to us with this chain. His hadith says: Ubaydullah ibn Miqsam informed me, from Abu Salih, and he added: 'One who drowns is a martyr.'

Hamid ibn Umar al-Bakrawi narrated to us: Abd al-Wahid (Ibn Ziyad) narrated to us: Asim narrated to us, from Hafsah bint Sirin, who said: Anas ibn Malik asked me: What did Yahya ibn Abi Amrah die of? I said: Plague. She said: He said that the Messenger of Allah said: Plague is martyrdom for every Muslim.
al-Walid ibn Shuja narrated this to us: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Asim, with this chain and a similar report.

Harun ibn Maruf informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu Ali Thumamah ibn Shufayy, who heard Uqbah ibn Amir say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, while he was on the pulpit, say: 'Prepare against them whatever strength you can.' Indeed, strength is archery. Indeed, strength is archery. Indeed, strength is archery.

Harun ibn Maruf narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu Ali, from Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: Lands will be opened up to you, and Allah will suffice you, so let none of you neglect to practice with his arrows.

Dawud ibn Rushayd narrated this to us: al-Walid narrated to us, from Bakr ibn Mudar, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Abu Ali al-Hamdani, who said: I heard Uqbah ibn Amir narrate from the Prophet with a similar report.

Muhammad ibn Rumh ibn al-Muhajir informed us: al-Layth informed us, from al-Harith ibn Yaqoub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Shumasah, that Fuqaym al-Lakhmi said to Uqbah ibn Amir: You keep going back and forth between these two targets, though you are old and it is difficult for you. Uqbah said: Were it not for something I heard from the Messenger of Allah, I would not do this. al-Harith said: I asked Ibn Shumasah: What was it? He said: The Prophet said: Whoever learns archery and then abandons it is not one of us—or he said: has disobeyed.

Said ibn Mansur, Abu al-Rabi al-Ataki, and Qutaybah ibn Said said: Hammad (Ibn Zayd) narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma, from Thawban, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: A group of my community will continue to remain manifest upon the truth. Those who forsake them will not harm them, until Allah's command comes while they are still in that state. Qutaybah's hadith does not include: 'while they are still in that state.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Waki and Abdah narrated to us, both from Ismail ibn Abi Khalid. [Another chain:] Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us (the wording is his): Marwan (al-Fazari) narrated to us, from Ismail, from Qays, from al-Mughirah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: A group of my community will continue to prevail over people until Allah's command comes to them while they are prevailing.
